2026-12-29.title: 29 December · Fifth Day within the Octave of Christmas
readings: Whoever loves a brother or sister lives in the light
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice
A light for revelation to the Gentiles
2026-12-29.alt: Optional memorial: St Thomas Becket, bishop and martyr. Liturgical colour: white.
2026-12-29.verse: Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.
theo: Old Simeon, “righteous and devout, looking forward to the consolation of Israel”, had been promised by the Holy Spirit that he would not die before seeing the Lord's Messiah. Guided by the Spirit he comes into the Temple just as Mary and Joseph bring in the child. He takes Jesus in his arms and sings the Nunc Dimittis, which the Church prays every night at Compline: now I can die in peace, for I have seen your salvation.

Simeon's song is universal: the child is “a light for revelation to the Gentiles” as well as the glory of Israel. But he also speaks of contradiction: the child will be “a sign that will be opposed”, and a sword will pierce Mary's soul. The first reading draws the practical lesson: “whoever says, ‘I abide in him,’ ought to walk just as he walked”; whoever loves a brother or sister lives in the light. St Thomas Becket, archbishop of Canterbury, killed in his cathedral on this day in 1170, gave his life defending the freedom of the Church.
outline: Ask: what are you waiting for in life? Simeon waited for one thing.
Simeon comes at the right moment.
Christ divides hearts; the sword pierces Mary.
live: Pray the Nunc Dimittis
Pray Simeon's song before sleeping tonight.
Walk in the light (1 John 2:10)
Make peace with someone you have avoided.
2026-12-29.prayer: Lord, now let your servant go in peace; your word has been fulfilled. My eyes have seen the salvation you prepared for all peoples. Let me walk in your light and love my brothers and sisters. Amen.
altar: Like Simeon, at each Mass we receive Christ into our arms and hearts. Our eyes have seen his salvation.

2026-12-30.title: 30 December · Sixth Day within the Octave of Christmas
readings: Whoever does the will of God lives forever
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice
Anna spoke about the child to all who were looking for redemption
2026-12-30.verse: At that moment she came, and began to praise God and to speak about the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.
theo: After Simeon comes Anna, a prophet, the daughter of Phanuel of the tribe of Asher, a widow of great age. She “never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day.” A whole life of faithful prayer prepares her to recognise the child at once. She becomes one of the first evangelists: she praises God and speaks about the child to everyone waiting for redemption.

Luke places a man and a woman, Simeon and Anna, side by side as witnesses; both elderly, both full of the Spirit. The elderly have a mission in the Church: to pray, to remember and to pass on the faith (Pope Francis, catecheses on old age, 2022). The first reading warns that “the world and its desire are passing away, but those who do the will of God live forever.” Then the Holy Family returns to Nazareth, and “the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom”.
outline: Ask: who taught you to pray? Many of us would name a grandmother.
Anna's long life of prayer and fasting.
Point 2 · She spoke about the child
The first woman to proclaim him in the Temple.
“The favor of God was upon him.”
live: Honour the elderly (Luke 2:36–37)
Thank an older person who taught you the faith.
Speak of Jesus (Luke 2:38)
Share with one person what Christmas means to you.
2026-12-30.prayer: Lord, give me Anna's faithfulness in prayer and her joy in speaking of your Son. Keep me from loving what is passing away, and let me do your will, that I may live forever. Amen.
altar: At Mass we join Anna in praising God for the Child, and speak of him to all who are waiting.

2026-12-31.title: 31 December · Seventh Day within the Octave of Christmas
readings: You have been anointed by the Holy One
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice
2026-12-31.alt: Optional memorial: St Sylvester I, pope. Liturgical colour: white. In the evening the Vigil Mass of the Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God, is celebrated.
2026-12-31.verse: From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace.
theo: On the last day of the civil year the Church reads again the Prologue of John: “In the beginning was the Word.” As one year ends and another begins, we remember the One who stands above all time, through whom “all things came into being”, and who entered time to give us “grace upon grace”. The first reading says: “Children, it is the last hour.” Christian time is not an endless circle; it moves towards Christ's return.

It is right to end the year with thanksgiving. The Church traditionally sings the Te Deum on this evening, and grants a plenary indulgence, under the usual conditions, to those who take part in its public recitation on the last day of the year (Enchiridion of Indulgences). We thank God for every grace of the past year, ask pardon for our sins, and entrust the new year to Mary, Mother of God, whose solemnity begins tonight. Pope St Sylvester I, remembered today, led the Church in the years after the persecutions ended.
outline: Ask: what are you most thankful for this year?
Christ is Lord of all time.
Whatever darkness this year held, the light was not overcome.
Count the graces; begin the new year in Christ.
“From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace.”
live: Give thanks
Write down five graces of this year and thank God for each.
Join the Te Deum
Take part in the thanksgiving service in your parish tonight.
2026-12-31.prayer: We praise you, O God, we acknowledge you to be the Lord. For every grace of this year, thank you; for every sin, forgive us; for the year to come, guide us. From your fullness let us receive grace upon grace. Amen.
altar: At this last Mass of the year we give thanks, which is what Eucharist means. From his fullness we receive grace upon grace.

quick: God's first word is comfort.
Repentance prepares the road for the Lord.
John points away from himself to Christ.
2026-12-06.action: Make an Advent Confession this week.
2026-12-06.question: Which mountain of pride or valley of discouragement needs levelling in me?
2026-12-06.special: Second Sunday of Advent, Year B. Colour: violet.
illus: An illustration
Before a bishop's visit to a Kerala parish, the road to the church is repaired, potholes filled, branches cut back, arches put up. We do all that for a bishop. What road are we preparing for Christ?

family.explain: John the Baptist told people to get ready for Jesus by saying sorry for their sins. We get ready the same way: by Confession and by being kind.
family.intention: We pray for courage to say sorry to God and to one another.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we clean up in our hearts and our home this week?”

kidsaint: A governor who became bishop of Milan by surprise, when a child in the crowd shouted, “Ambrose for bishop!” He later baptised St Augustine. Lesson: God can call us when we least expect it.
term: Greek for a “change of mind”: turning the whole person back to God. It is the first word of John's and Jesus' preaching.

pm.open: Comfort, O comfort my people, says your God. Lord, as we gather on this Second Sunday of Advent, prepare the way in our hearts for your Son. Amen.
share: Isaiah cries: prepare the way of the Lord (Isaiah 40:3). What mountain of pride or valley of discouragement needs levelling in me?
Peter says God is patient, not wanting any to perish (2 Peter 3:9). How have I experienced God's patience?
John the Baptist called people to confess their sins (Mark 1:5). When will I go to confession this Advent?
pm.resp: Prepare the way of the Lord.
interc: For the Church, that like John the Baptist she may prepare the way of the Lord.
For those who need comfort, that they may hear God's tender voice.
For sinners, that they may turn to God this Advent.
For our country, that justice and peace may be found on its paths.
For our families, that we may prepare our hearts more than our houses.
pm.close: Lord God, you speak tenderly to your people. Level the mountains of our pride, fill the valleys of our discouragement, and make straight the path for your Son. Amen.

quick: Joy is the heart of Advent: the Lord is near.
Christ fulfilled Isaiah's good news to the poor.
He stands among us, often unrecognised.
2026-12-13.action: Name three reasons for joy each night this week.
2026-12-13.question: Where is Christ among us whom I do not recognise?
2026-12-13.special: Third Sunday of Advent, Gaudete Sunday. Colour: rose or violet.
illus: An illustration
In Kerala homes the Christmas star goes up in the middle of Advent, before the feast itself. It does not mean Christmas has come; it announces that it is near. That is Gaudete Sunday.

family.explain: John the Baptist was a voice telling everyone that Jesus was near. He said Jesus was already among them, though they did not know him.
family.intention: We pray to recognise Jesus in each other.
family.ask: Ask: “Where did we see Jesus this week in someone's kindness?”

kidsaint: A young girl of Sicily who gave her riches to the poor and died a martyr. Her name means “light”. Lesson: be a light for others.
term: Latin for “Rejoice!”; the name of the Third Sunday of Advent, from the Entrance Antiphon (Philippians 4:4).

pm.open: Rejoice in the Lord always; again I say, rejoice. The Lord is near. Lord Jesus, on this Gaudete Sunday fill our gathering with your joy. Amen.
share: Paul says: rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances (1 Thessalonians 5:16–18). Which of these is hardest for me?
John said: I am not the Messiah (John 1:20). How do I point others to Jesus rather than to myself?
What gives me true joy this Advent?
pm.resp: Rejoice in the Lord always.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a witness of joy in a sad world.
For those who cannot rejoice because of grief, illness or poverty.
For the poor and the brokenhearted, to whom good news is promised (Isaiah 61:1).
For prisoners and captives, that they may find freedom.
For our group, that we may rejoice, pray and give thanks always.
pm.close: Lord God, the coming of your Son is near. Fill us with joy, teach us to give thanks in all things, and make us witnesses to the light. Amen.

quick: David wanted to build God a house; God built David a house.
In Mary the promise to David is fulfilled.
Mary's yes is the obedience of faith.
2026-12-20.action: Pray the Angelus three times a day this week.
2026-12-20.question: What is God asking me to say yes to before Christmas?
2026-12-20.special: Fourth Sunday of Advent, Year B. Colour: violet.
illus: An illustration
In Kerala, when a family builds a new house, the first thing placed inside is often a picture of the Holy Family or the Sacred Heart. David wanted to build God a house; God wanted to live in ours.

family.explain: The angel Gabriel asked Mary to be the mother of Jesus. Mary said yes to God. In a few days we will celebrate the birth of her Son.
family.intention: We pray to say yes to God like Mary.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family make room for Jesus this Christmas?”

kidsaint: A Jesuit priest who wrote simple catechisms so children could learn their faith. Lesson: learning about God helps us love him.
term: The announcement by the angel Gabriel to Mary that she would conceive the Son of God by the Holy Spirit (Luke 1:26–38).

pm.open: Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you. Lord God, on this last Sunday of Advent, give us Mary's faith to say yes to your word. Amen.
share: David wanted to build God a house, but God promised to build David a house (2 Samuel 7:11). How has God done more for me than I could do for him?
Mary asked: how can this be? (Luke 1:34). What question do I bring to God?
Mary said: let it be with me according to your word (Luke 1:38). Where must I say yes?
pm.resp: Let it be done to us according to your word.
interc: For the Church, that like Mary she may welcome God's word.
For expectant mothers, that they may be safe and joyful.
For the homeless, that God may provide them a house.
For all who find God's will hard to accept.
For our families, as we prepare for Christmas.
pm.close: Lord God, you chose the Virgin Mary to be the Mother of your Son. With her, we say: here we are, the servants of the Lord. Let it be done to us according to your word. Amen.

quick: The eternal Word became flesh and lived among us.
God's final word to us is a Child.
To all who receive him he gives power to become children of God.
2026-12-25.action: Invite someone lonely to share your Christmas meal.
2026-12-25.question: Is there room for Jesus in my inn?
2026-12-25.special: Solemnity of the Nativity of the Lord. Holy day of obligation. Colour: white.
illus: An illustration

In Kerala the Christmas star hangs on every Christian house, and carol groups go from home to home through the night. The star tells the street: here people believe God has come. The carols tell the world: rejoice!

family.explain: God the Son became a little baby, born of Mary in Bethlehem. He came because he loves us and wants us to be God's children.
family.intention: We thank God for sending Jesus and pray for families who are poor or alone at Christmas.
family.ask: Ask: “What birthday gift can we give Jesus this year?”

kidsaint: He set up the first Christmas crib in 1223 so that people could see how poor and little Jesus became for us. Lesson: Jesus came as a little child so that no one would be afraid of him.
term: The mystery that the eternal Son of God took a human nature and became man, without ceasing to be God (CCC 461–463).

pm.open: Glory to God in the highest, and peace to his people on earth. Lord Jesus, born for us today, we gather with joy around your crib. Amen.
share: The Word became flesh and lived among us (John 1:14). What does it mean to me that God became one of us?
How beautiful are the feet of the messenger who brings good news (Isaiah 52:7). How can I bring good news to someone today?
What gift will I give the Child this Christmas?
pm.resp: Glory to God in the highest.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the good news of great joy.
For peace in the world, especially in the land where Jesus was born.
For families, that the Prince of Peace may dwell in their homes.
For the poor, the homeless and refugees, who share the poverty of the manger.
For the sick, the lonely and the grieving on this day.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, eternal Word made flesh, fill our hearts with your light and peace, and make us messengers of your good news. Amen.

quick: The Son of God grew up in a family.
Abraham and Sarah show that families are built on faith.
Nazareth makes ordinary family life holy.
2026-12-27.action: Pray together as a family this evening, even for ten minutes.
2026-12-27.question: Is God at the centre of my home?
2026-12-27.special: Feast of the Holy Family, Year B. Colour: white.
illus: An illustration

In many Kerala homes the family gathers in the evening before a lamp and a picture of the Holy Family for the family rosary. Children who fall asleep during it still remember, years later, that their parents knelt.

family.explain: Jesus grew up in a family with Mary and Joseph in Nazareth. He obeyed them, helped them, prayed with them and grew strong and wise.
family.intention: We pray for our family and for all families, especially those who are broken or suffering.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we can do to make our home more like the home at Nazareth?”

kidsaint: The quiet carpenter who protected Mary and Jesus and taught Jesus his trade. Lesson: we help our family by doing our daily work with love.
term: The Christian family, where the faith is first received, prayed and lived (CCC 1655–1658).

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you grew in wisdom and grace in the home of Mary and Joseph. On this feast of the Holy Family, bless our families. Amen.
share: Abraham believed God's promise when it seemed impossible (Genesis 15:6). What promise of God do I hold on to for my family?
Simeon and Anna waited faithfully for years (Luke 2:25, 36–37). What can the elderly teach my family?
What would make our home more like Nazareth?
pm.resp: Jesus, Mary and Joseph, bless our family.
interc: For all families, that they may imitate the Holy Family.
For grandparents and the elderly, like Simeon and Anna.
For families separated by migration.
For couples who long for a child.
For broken families, that they may find healing.
pm.close: Lord God, you gave your Son a home in Nazareth. Bless our families with faith, love and patience, and keep us united in you. Amen.

quick: God brings new life from a cut-down stump.
The Spirit of the Lord rests on the Messiah.
God reveals himself to the little ones.
2026-12-01.action: Pray each day for one gift of the Holy Spirit.
2026-12-01.question: Am I too “wise” to receive what God reveals to the little ones?

family.explain: Isaiah saw a new branch growing from an old stump, and animals living in peace. Jesus brings new life and peace, and a little child leads them.
family.intention: We pray for peace in our home and in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “Where do we need God's peace in our family this Advent?”

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, who rested on the shoot of Jesse. As we begin Advent, fill us with your gifts and make us little children before the Father. Amen.
share: Isaiah speaks of a shoot from a stump (Isaiah 11:1). What in my life looks finished, and could God bring it back to life?
Jesus says the Father reveals his secrets to infants (Luke 10:21). Where do I need to become little again?
Which gift of the Holy Spirit do I most need this Advent?
pm.resp: Come, Lord Jesus, Prince of Peace.
interc: For the Church, that she may be renewed by the Holy Spirit this Advent.
For places of war and hatred, that the peace of Isaiah's vision may come.
For those who feel their life is finished, that God may make new shoots spring up.
For children, that they may lead us to simplicity and trust.
For our group, that we may grow in the gifts of the Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you revealed your Son to the little ones. Make us humble and open, fill us with the Spirit of wisdom and peace, and prepare us to welcome Jesus at Christmas. Amen.

illus: An illustration

After a cyclone flattened a coconut grove near Alappuzha, the farmer thought everything was lost. Weeks later he noticed green shoots rising from the stumps of trees he had given up for dead. He said: “God showed me Advent in my own field.”

quick: God promises a feast and the end of death.
Jesus' compassion heals and feeds.
Christ multiplies what we bring and asks us to share it.
2026-12-02.action: Give a meal or groceries to a needy family.
2026-12-02.question: Do I give thanks for my daily bread?

family.explain: Jesus felt sorry for the hungry people and fed them with only seven loaves. When we share the little we have, Jesus makes it enough.
family.intention: We pray for children and families who are hungry.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share with someone in need this Advent?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you had compassion on the hungry crowd. As we gather, heal our wounds, feed us with your word and teach us to share our bread. Amen.
share: Isaiah promises that God will wipe away every tear (Isaiah 25:8). What tears do I bring to the Lord today?
The disciples saw what they lacked; Jesus asked what they had. What ‘loaves’ can I offer?
Who around me is hungry, in body or in spirit?
pm.resp: Lord, have compassion on your people.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a place of healing and feeding for all peoples.
For the hungry and the poor, that they may find bread and dignity.
For the sick, the disabled and the suffering, that Christ may heal them.
For those who grieve, that God may wipe away their tears.
For our parish, that our Advent sharing may be generous.
pm.close: Lord God, you prepare a banquet for all peoples. Make us generous with the little we have, so that through us many may be fed, until we sit together at your table in the Kingdom. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A parish in Kochi began collecting one packet of rice from each family every Advent Sunday. The first year they hoped for a hundred packets. They received over a thousand. A parishioner said: “We gave seven loaves; God made it four thousand.”

quick: Saying “Lord, Lord” is not enough; we must do his will.
Build on the Rock, and the storms will not destroy you.
Francis Xavier built his life on Christ and carried him across Asia.
2026-12-03.action: Act on one teaching of Jesus you have been ignoring.
2026-12-03.question: What is my life really built on?

family.explain: Jesus says a wise person builds a house on rock. When we listen to Jesus and do what he says, our lives are strong.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries, especially those from India.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing Jesus says that we can do this week?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, rock of our salvation, you gave St Francis Xavier a heart on fire for the Gospel. As we gather, help us not only to hear your word but to build our lives on it. Amen.
share: Jesus says not everyone who says Lord, Lord will enter (Matthew 7:21). Where is my faith more words than action?
What ‘storms’ have tested the foundations of my life?
What word of Jesus will I put into practice this week?
pm.resp: Lord, you are our rock.
interc: For missionaries throughout the world, that they may be faithful and fruitful.
For the people of India's coasts, evangelised by St Francis Xavier.
For those whose lives have been shaken by storms, that they may find a firm foundation in Christ.
For vocations to the missionary life.
For our families, that they may be built on the rock of God's word.
pm.close: Lord God, through St Francis Xavier you brought the Gospel to our land. Make us doers of your word, built on the rock of your Son, and give us his zeal to share our faith. Amen.

illus: An illustration

During the 2018 Kerala floods, an old house built by a grandfather on a raised stone foundation stood untouched while newer houses around it were damaged. The grandson said: “He spent more on what nobody sees: the foundation.”

quick: God promises that the blind will see.
Jesus asks: Do you believe I can do this?
Faith sees before the eyes do.
2026-12-04.action: Spend time before the Blessed Sacrament this First Friday.
2026-12-04.question: Do I really believe Jesus can change my situation?

family.explain: Two blind men asked Jesus for mercy, and because they believed, he healed them.
family.intention: We pray for people who are blind or sick, and for anyone who cannot see God's love.
family.ask: Ask: “Do we believe Jesus can help us? What shall we ask him for?”

pm.open: Sacred Heart of Jesus, on this First Friday we cry with the blind men: Son of David, have mercy on us. Open our eyes to your love. Amen.
share: Jesus asks: do you believe that I am able to do this? (Matthew 9:28). What do I find hard to believe Jesus can do?
What is my blindness: to God, to others, or to myself?
How will I honour the Sacred Heart this First Friday?
pm.resp: Son of David, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the mercy of the Heart of Jesus.
For the blind, the deaf and all with disabilities, that they may be respected and helped.
For those spiritually blind, that their eyes may be opened.
For sinners, that they may find mercy in confession this Advent.
For our families, that we may see one another's needs.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you opened the eyes of the blind. Touch our hearts and our eyes, and let it be done to us according to our faith. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A businessman in Thrissur said he had never noticed the beggar outside his office for ten years. One First Friday, after confession, he stopped, talked with the man and learnt his name. “I was the blind one,” he said.

quick: God waits to be gracious and hears our cry.
Jesus has compassion on the harassed and helpless.
What we received freely, we give freely.
2026-12-05.action: Pray daily for vocations this Advent.
2026-12-05.question: What have I received freely that I could give freely?

family.explain: Jesus felt sorry for people who were lost, like sheep without a shepherd. He asks us to pray for helpers and to help others too.
family.intention: We pray for priests, sisters and catechists.
family.ask: Ask: “What have we received from God that we can share with others?”

pm.open: Lord of the harvest, you look with compassion on the crowds. As we gather, let us hear your voice saying: this is the way; walk in it. Amen.
share: Isaiah promises a word behind us: this is the way (Isaiah 30:21). Where do I need God's guidance now?
Jesus saw the crowds as sheep without a shepherd (Matthew 9:36). Whom do I see like that?
What have I received freely that I can give freely?
pm.resp: Lord, send labourers into your harvest.
interc: For vocations to the priesthood and religious life.
For catechists and Sunday school teachers.
For people who are harassed and helpless, that they may find a shepherd.
For those in adversity, that God may be gracious to them at the sound of their cry.
For our group, that we may be generous labourers in the harvest.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, good Shepherd, you sent your apostles to heal and proclaim. Send us too, and make us generous with what we have freely received. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A retired schoolteacher in Kottayam began tutoring children from a nearby colony every evening without charge. When asked why, she said: “I received my education almost free from the sisters. I am just giving back what I received.”

quick: God makes the desert bloom.
Friends' faith brings the paralysed man to Jesus.
Christ's first healing is forgiveness.
2026-12-07.action: Pray daily for a friend who needs Jesus.
2026-12-07.question: Whom am I carrying to Jesus?

family.explain: Four friends carried a man who could not walk to Jesus. Jesus forgave his sins and healed him. We can bring our friends to Jesus by praying for them.
family.intention: We pray for a friend or relative who needs Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we ‘carry’ to Jesus in our prayer this week?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you saw the faith of those who carried their friend. As we gather, we bring to you all those we love who cannot come by themselves. Amen.
share: Jesus saw their faith (Luke 5:20). Whose faith has carried me to Jesus?
Whom am I carrying in prayer, and have I given up too soon?
Isaiah says: be strong, do not fear (Isaiah 35:4). What fear do I need to hand over?
pm.resp: Lord, heal and forgive us.
interc: For the Church, that she may carry the weak and the paralysed to Christ.
For bishops, that like St Ambrose they may lead many to Christ.
For the sick and disabled, that they may find healing and dignity.
For those far from the faith, that our prayer may carry them home.
For all who are afraid, that they may hear: here is your God.
pm.close: Lord God, through St Ambrose you led Augustine to faith. Strengthen our weak hands and feeble knees, and make us faithful in carrying others to your Son. Amen.

illus: An illustration

For twelve years a mother in Thalassery prayed every day for her son who had left the Church. Her prayer group prayed with her. One Christmas he came home and went to confession. She said: “We were the four men on the roof.”

quick: Mary was preserved from original sin from her first moment.
She was redeemed by Christ, in the most perfect way.
Grace freed her to say yes.
2026-12-08.action: Pray the Hail Mary slowly, phrase by phrase.
2026-12-08.question: Where am I when God calls me?
2026-12-08.special: Solemnity of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary. Colour: white.
illus: An illustration
Before a new house is blessed in Kerala, it is cleaned, painted and decorated so that it is ready. God did even more: he prepared Mary from the very beginning, so that his Son would find a pure home.

family.explain: God made Mary pure and full of grace from the very first moment of her life, because she was going to be Jesus' mother. Mary said yes to God.
family.intention: We ask Mary to help our family say yes to God.
family.ask: Ask: “What is God asking our family to say yes to this Advent?”

kidsaint: A poor, sickly girl to whom Mary appeared in 1858 and said, “I am the Immaculate Conception.” Bernadette did not know what it meant, but she repeated it faithfully. Lesson: God speaks to the little ones.
term: The dogma that Mary, from the first moment of her conception, was preserved free from original sin by God's grace, in view of the merits of Christ (CCC 491).

pm.open: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with you. On this feast of your Immaculate Conception we gather with joy. Pray for us, that our hearts may be made ready for your Son. Amen.
share: God preserved Mary from all sin from the first moment (Ephesians 1:4). What does Mary's purity teach me?
Adam and Eve hid from God (Genesis 3:10). Where am I hiding from God?
Mary said: let it be with me according to your word (Luke 1:38). Where must I say yes this Advent?
pm.resp: Holy Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that she may be holy and without blemish like Mary.
For our country, that Mary may lead all its people to her Son.
For young people, that they may grow in purity of heart.
For sinners, that Mary may lead them to her Son's mercy.
For mothers, that Mary may guide and protect them.
pm.close: Father, you prepared a worthy dwelling for your Son in the Virgin Mary. Through her prayers, cleanse us from sin and make our hearts a home for Jesus. Amen.

quick: God never grows weary.
Jesus invites the weary to rest in him.
Those who wait on the Lord renew their strength.
2026-12-09.action: Hand over one burden to Jesus before the tabernacle.
2026-12-09.question: What burden am I carrying without Jesus?

family.explain: Jesus says: come to me when you are tired, and I will give you rest. He is gentle and kind.
family.intention: We pray for parents, grandparents and all who are tired.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we help someone in our family who is tired this week?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, gentle and humble of heart, you call the weary to yourself. As we gather, we bring you our burdens; give us your rest. Amen.
share: Isaiah says God calls the stars by name (Isaiah 40:26). How does it feel to know God knows me by name?
Jesus says: come to me, all who are weary (Matthew 11:28). What is my heaviest burden?
How can I make time to rest in the Lord this Advent?
pm.resp: Lord, give us your rest.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a place of rest for the weary.
For parents and caregivers who are exhausted.
For workers abroad and those in hard labour.
For the sick and the elderly, that they may renew their strength in the Lord.
For our group, that we may help carry one another's burdens.
pm.close: Lord God, you give power to the faint. Renew our strength, teach us to rest in your Son, and let us learn from his gentle and humble heart. Amen.

illus: An illustration
A nurse working night shifts in a Delhi hospital said: “On my way home every morning I stop for ten minutes at the chapel. I don't say much. I just give him the night. I leave lighter than I came.”

quick: God holds our right hand.
He opens rivers in the desert for the thirsty.
The least in the Kingdom is greater than John.
2026-12-10.action: Find and celebrate your baptism date.
2026-12-10.question: Do I let God hold my hand?

family.explain: God says: do not be afraid, I will help you. Even when we feel small, God holds our hand.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who is afraid.
family.ask: Ask: “When do we feel small, and how does God help us?”

pm.open: Lord God, you hold us by the right hand and say: do not fear, I will help you. As we gather, turn our dryness into springs of living water. Amen.
share: God says: do not fear, I will help you (Isaiah 41:13). Where do I feel small and afraid?
Jesus says the least in the Kingdom is greater than John (Matthew 11:11). What great gifts have I received?
What dry place in my life needs God's water?
pm.resp: The Lord is our helper; we shall not fear.
interc: For the Church, that she may be grateful for the riches of the Kingdom.
For those who feel small and afraid, that God may hold their hand.
For regions suffering drought and water shortage.
For prophets and witnesses of truth in our time.
For our group, that we may use our gifts generously.
pm.close: Lord God, Holy One of Israel, you help the weak and make the desert bloom. Hold us by the hand, and make us fruitful with the gifts of your Kingdom. Amen.

illus: An illustration
A small girl in a Kerala parish was asked why she gave her birthday money to the Advent collection for the poor. She said: “Jesus gave me everything. I'm only little, but I can give a little.”

quick: God's commandments lead to peace like a river.
Some hearts make excuses against every messenger.
Wisdom is shown by its fruit.
2026-12-11.action: Drop one excuse you use with God.
2026-12-11.question: Am I dancing when God plays the flute?

family.explain: God teaches us his commandments because he loves us. When we obey, our peace flows like a river.
family.intention: We pray that our family may listen to God's word with open hearts.
family.ask: Ask: “What excuses do we sometimes make when God asks something of us?”

pm.open: Lord our God, you teach us for our own good. As we gather, open our hearts to your word, and free us from the excuses that keep us from you. Amen.
share: God says: O that you had paid attention to my commandments (Isaiah 48:18). Which commandment do I find hardest?
What excuses do I make to avoid responding to God?
Jesus says wisdom is vindicated by her deeds (Matthew 11:19). What fruit does my faith show?
pm.resp: Lord, lead us in your way.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim God's commandments as a path of life.
For those who reject God with excuses, that their hearts may be opened.
For young people, that they may find God's way for their lives.
For those without peace, that it may flow like a river.
For our group, that our faith may bear good fruit.
pm.close: Lord God, you lead us in the way we should go. Free us from excuses, open our hearts to your word, and let our lives show the wisdom of your Son. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A young man complained that every parish he tried was wrong: the music, the sermons, the people. An old priest told him: “Son, you will never find the perfect parish. But if you stop looking for faults, you may find God.” He stayed, and found both friends and faith.

quick: Elijah was a prophet like fire.
Elijah returned in John, and many did not recognise him.
Mary of Guadalupe carries Christ to a whole people.
2026-12-12.action: Reconcile with a family member before Christmas.
2026-12-12.question: Do I recognise the messengers God sends me?

family.explain: Elijah spoke God's word like fire. He helped parents and children love each other again. Mary, Our Lady of Guadalupe, loves all mothers and children.
family.intention: We pray for mothers and unborn babies.
family.ask: Ask: “How can parents and children in our family spend more time together?”

pm.open: Lord God, you sent Elijah, John and Mary to prepare the way for your Son. As we gather, turn our hearts to you and to one another. Amen.
share: Elijah's word burned like a torch (Sirach 48:1). What word of God burns in my heart?
Jesus says they did not recognise Elijah (Matthew 17:12). Whom do I fail to recognise as God's messenger?
How can I turn my heart more to my family?
pm.resp: Our Lady of Guadalupe, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that she may speak God's truth with fire and tenderness.
For mothers and unborn children, through the prayers of Our Lady of Guadalupe.
For families where parents and children are distant, that their hearts may be turned.
For indigenous and tribal peoples, that they may be respected.
For our group, that we may recognise God's messengers in our lives.
pm.close: Lord God, through Our Lady of Guadalupe you showed a mother's love to the poor. Turn the hearts of parents to their children, and prepare us to welcome your Son. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A father in Bengaluru, always working late, decided one Advent to be home for dinner every evening. His teenage daughter, who had stopped talking to him, slowly began to share her day again. He said: “Elijah turned my heart to my child.”

quick: God's star rises even through an unexpected prophet.
Christ's authority is from heaven.
Truth asks for honesty, not calculation.
2026-12-14.action: Spend ten minutes in silent prayer.
2026-12-14.question: Which truth am I avoiding?

family.explain: Long ago a man saw a vision of a star that would come from Jacob. Christians believe this star is Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for people who are searching for God.
family.ask: Ask: “Are we brave enough to say we love Jesus, even when it is not easy?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Star of Jacob, you shine on all who seek you. As we gather, free us from calculation and fear, and give us honest hearts. Amen.
share: Balaam saw the star from afar (Numbers 24:17). How has Christ come near to me?
The leaders said: we do not know (Matthew 21:27). When do I avoid the truth because it is inconvenient?
What would it mean for me to give everything, like St John of the Cross?
pm.resp: Lord, let your light shine on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may speak the truth with courage.
For those who seek God sincerely, that the Star may guide them.
For contemplatives and Carmelites, through the prayers of St John of the Cross.
For leaders, that they may seek truth rather than popularity.
For our group, that we may be honest in our faith.
pm.close: Lord God, you showed Balaam the star from afar. Let your Son, the bright morning star, rise in our hearts, and give us courage to follow the truth. Amen.

illus: An illustration

A college student in Chennai was asked by friends whether she really believed in God. She was tempted to joke and avoid the question. Instead she said simply: “Yes, I do, and it has changed my life.” Two of them later asked her to take them to church.

quick: God's future belongs to the humble remnant.
Deeds matter more than words.
Repentant sinners enter the Kingdom first.
2026-12-15.action: Do something you earlier refused God.
2026-12-15.question: Is my “yes” to God only words?

family.explain: One son said no but then obeyed. The other said yes but did not go. Jesus wants us to do what we say.
family.intention: We pray that we may keep our promises to God and to each other.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something we said we would do but haven't done yet?”

pm.open: Lord God, you love the humble and lowly. As we gather, help us to change our minds and do your will, not only with words but with our lives. Amen.
share: Which son am I most like (Matthew 21:28–31)?
Where have I said yes to God but not acted?
Zephaniah speaks of a humble people (Zephaniah 3:12). What would humility look like in my life today?
pm.resp: Lord, we will do your will.
interc: For the Church, that she may be humble and lowly, seeking refuge in the Lord.
For sinners, that they may change their minds and return to God.
For those who keep faith only in words, that their lives may match their lips.
For the poor of the Lord, who wait for his coming.
For our group, that we may keep our promises.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today the prophet Isaiah begins with a beautiful word: “Comfort, O comfort my people.” After years of exile, God's first word is not anger but tenderness.

And then a voice cries out: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the Lord.” Every valley lifted up, every mountain made low. In ancient times roads were repaired before a king's visit. Isaiah says: God himself is coming; prepare his road!

Mark begins his Gospel with John the Baptist in the desert. People come from everywhere, confessing their sins and being baptised in the Jordan. That is how the road is prepared: not with decorations but with repentance.

What are the mountains in us? Pride, stubbornness, the refusal to forgive. What are the valleys? Discouragement, laziness, the feeling that I can never change. Advent asks us to bring both to God. Confession is the bulldozer that levels the road!
And John points away from himself: “One more powerful than I is coming… he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.” A true Christian is like John: a finger pointing to Jesus.

St Peter tells us why the Lord seems to delay: “The Lord is not slow about his promise, but is patient with you, not wanting any to perish.” This Advent is God's patience with us. Let us not waste it. Make a good Confession. Comfort someone who is low. And prepare the road for the King.
kids: Children, when an important guest is coming, what do we do? We clean the house!
John the Baptist told the people: Jesus is coming; clean your hearts!
How do we clean our hearts? By saying sorry to God in Confession, and sorry to people we have hurt.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Gaudete Sunday, the Sunday of joy. The priest may wear rose vestments, and we light the rose candle. Why? Because the Lord is near.

The prophet Isaiah says: “The spirit of the Lord is upon me; he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor, to bind up the broken-hearted, to proclaim liberty to captives.” Years later Jesus stood in the synagogue of Nazareth, read these words, and said: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled.” Our joy has a name: Jesus.

Instead of a psalm we sing Mary's song: “My soul rejoices in my God.” Mary was poor and humble, and God did great things for her. Christian joy is not the joy of having everything; it is the joy of being loved by God.

In the Gospel people ask John: “Who are you? Are you the Messiah? Elijah? The prophet?” And he says, “No, no, no. I am only a voice.” And then: “Among you stands one whom you do not know.” Jesus was already there, in the crowd, unnoticed.
Is it the same with us? Jesus is among us: in the Eucharist, in the Word, in the poor at our gate, in the family member we take for granted. Advent asks us to open our eyes.

St Paul gives us a simple programme for this week: “Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances.” Try it: every night, thank God for three joys. And remember his promise: “The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do this.” Rejoice: the Lord is near!
kids: Children, today the candle is pink, I mean rose! It's the candle of joy.
Christmas is getting close, and Jesus is near!
John the Baptist said: Jesus is among you, but you don't know him. Where can we find Jesus? In church, in our family, in poor people.
This week, say thank you to God for three happy things every night!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this last Sunday before Christmas, the readings tell us about two houses.

King David lived in a palace of cedar. He looked at the ark of God in a tent and felt ashamed: “I live in luxury and God lives in a tent. Let me build God a house.” A good thought. But God answers through the prophet Nathan: “You will build me a house? No, I will build you a house.” God promises David a family line whose throne will last forever.

A thousand years later, in a small village called Nazareth, the angel Gabriel greets a young woman: “You will conceive and bear a son… The Lord God will give him the throne of his ancestor David, and of his kingdom there will be no end.” The promise to David comes true, not in a palace but in a girl's humble home.

Mary asks, “How can this be?” Not doubt, but faith seeking to understand. The angel answers: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you.” Just as God's cloud rested on the tent in the desert, God now rests on Mary. She becomes the house of God, the true Ark of the Covenant.

And then her answer: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” With these words, the whole history of salvation turns. St Bernard imagined the whole world holding its breath, waiting for her yes.

Like David, we often want to do great things for God. But God wants first to do great things in us. This Christmas, he asks to make his home in our hearts. Let us make room, like Mary, and say: “Let it be with me according to your word.”
kids: Children, King David wanted to build a big house for God. But God said: I will build a house for you!
Then God chose Mary to be the mother of Jesus. Mary said yes to God.
Jesus wants to live in our hearts too. Can we say yes like Mary?
This week, help set up the crib at home, and leave the manger empty until Christmas night!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a happy and holy Christmas to you all!

Tonight and today the Church tells the story three ways. At night, Luke tells us of the census, the journey to Bethlehem, no room in the inn, the manger, the shepherds and the angels singing, “Glory to God in the highest.” In the day, John lifts our eyes to eternity: “In the beginning was the Word… and the Word became flesh and lived among us.”

Who is this child? Not just a good man, not an angel, but God himself. The eternal Son, through whom everything was made, now lies in a manger, needing his mother's milk. St Augustine marvelled: the Bread was hungry, the Fountain was thirsty, the Light slept. God became small so that we would not be afraid to come close.

Why did he come? The letter to the Hebrews says: long ago God spoke through the prophets, but now he has spoken to us by a Son. Christmas is God's final word to us, and that word is love in the form of a child. He came to forgive our sins, to show us the Father, and to make us God's own children. St John says: “To all who received him, he gave power to become children of God.”

But there was no room in the inn. Is there room in ours? In our busy celebrations, our shopping, our food and decorations, is there room for the Child? And is there room for the poor, the lonely, the migrant, those for whom this Christmas is sad?

Bethlehem means “House of Bread”. The Child was laid in a manger, where animals eat. From the beginning he was preparing to give himself as our food. Today at this altar he comes to us again. Let us receive him with joy, and, as St Leo said, “Christian, remember your dignity.” A blessed Christmas to you and your families!
kids: Children, Happy Birthday, Jesus!
God loves us so much that he became a tiny baby, born in a stable because there was no room for him.
The angels sang, the shepherds came running, and Mary held baby Jesus close.
What gift can you give Jesus today? A kind heart! Share a sweet, hug your family, and say thank you, Jesus!

intro: Bethlehem means house of bread. The Child born there was laid in a manger, a feeding trough. From the first day, He offered Himself as food.

sub: Bethlehem: Beth-lehem, house of bread.
God chose the town's name with care.
The Bread of Life is born in the House of Bread.
points.apply: At Communion today, remember Bethlehem.

sub: A manger is where animals eat.
The Child is placed where food is placed.
Christmas leads to the Holy Mass.
points.apply: Kneel at the crib and then at the altar with the same faith.

sub: The shepherds came and shared the news.
Christmas joy grows when shared.
Feed someone who is hungry this Christmas.
points.apply: Share a meal or a gift with a poor family.

concl: The Child of Bethlehem continues to give Himself as Bread on our altars.
Christmas is fulfilled when we receive Him and share Him.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will receive Communion with the faith of the shepherds and share my bread with someone in need.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a joyful and blessed Christmas to all of you! Tonight let us go in spirit to a small town in Judea. Its name was Bethlehem. In Hebrew, Bethlehem means house of bread. It was there, and nowhere else, that God chose to be born.

The prophet Micah had foretold it: from you, Bethlehem, small among the clans of Judah, shall come forth one who is to rule in Israel (Micah 5:2). God plans with care. The One who would say I am the bread of life (John 6:35) was born in the house of bread.

And where did Mary lay Him? In a manger (Luke 2:7). We have made the crib beautiful with lights and decorations, but a manger was a feeding trough, the place where animals came to eat. The prophet Isaiah had said that the ox knows its owner and the donkey its master's crib, but Israel does not understand (Isaiah 1:3). The Son of God was placed where food is placed. From His first night on earth He was saying: I have come to be your food.

That is why Christmas leads us to the altar. In a few moments, on this altar, the same Christ born in Bethlehem will become present under the appearance of bread. The shepherds knelt at the manger; we kneel before the Holy Mass. They saw a child; we see bread. In both cases faith sees God hidden in humility. Receive Him tonight with the faith of the shepherds.

And the shepherds did not keep the good news to themselves. They told everyone what they had heard (Luke 2:17). Bread is meant to be shared. This Christmas, share your bread with someone who is hungry, lonely or forgotten: a meal, a visit, a phone call. Then Christmas will not end tonight. It will continue in every house where Christ, the Bread of Life, is received and shared.

opts.a: Teaching homily: the Incarnation, true God and true man
intro: Christmas is not only a sweet story. It is the heart of our faith: God became man.

sub: The eternal Son took a human nature (John 1:14).
Not a phantom, not a half-god.
For us and for our salvation (Nicene Creed).
points.apply: Bow deeply at the words of the Creed: and became man.

sub: One divine Person, two natures (CCC 464–469).
Councils of Nicaea, Ephesus, Chalcedon.
Mary is truly Mother of God, Theotokos (CCC 495).
points.apply: Call Mary Mother of God with faith in the Hail Mary.

sub: To reconcile us with God (CCC 457).
To show us God's love (CCC 458).
To be our model of holiness and to make us sharers in the divine nature (CCC 459–460).
points.apply: Thank God that He came to make you His child.

concl: The Incarnation is the greatest proof of God's love.
God became man so that we might share His divine life.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will bow at the words of the Creed and thank God for becoming man.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed Christmas to you all! We have heard the familiar story again: the journey, the manger, the shepherds. But behind the story is the most astonishing truth ever proclaimed: God became man. Tonight let us look at this mystery as the Church teaches it.

St John writes: in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God; and the Word became flesh and lived among us (John 1:1, 14). The Child in the manger is not a good man whom God later adopted, nor a god who only seemed human. He is the eternal Son of God who took to Himself a full human nature, body and soul, in the womb of the Virgin Mary. That is why, in the Creed, at the words and became man, we bow; on Christmas day, we kneel.

The early Church had to defend this truth against many errors. The Councils of Nicaea, Ephesus and Chalcedon taught that Jesus Christ is one divine Person in two natures, divine and human, without confusion and without separation (CCC 464–469). Because the Child is God, the Council of Ephesus proclaimed Mary Theotokos, Mother of God (CCC 495). This is not an exaggeration about Mary; it is a protection of the truth about Jesus.

Why did God become man? The Catechism gives four reasons. To save us by reconciling us with God. So that we might know God's love. To be our model of holiness. And to make us partakers of the divine nature (CCC 457–460; 2 Peter 1:4). The Fathers of the Church summed it up: the Son of God became a son of man so that we might become children of God.

So Christmas is not only for children; it is the foundation of our whole faith. At this Holy Mass the same Word made flesh comes to us. Let us receive Him with wonder, and let His love, so humble and so close, change the way we live.

opts.a: Peace on earth: the angels' song and our reconciliation
intro: On the night of the Nativity the sky over Bethlehem was filled with an army of angels singing glory to God and peace on earth (Luke 2:13–14). Two thousand years later the world still longs for that peace: in the Holy Land where Christ was born, in every land torn by war or communal conflict, and in many of our own homes.
Tonight the Prince of Peace is born. He does not bring peace by force, but by coming close to us, small and defenceless.

sub: Peace is first a gift from God, not an agreement among people.
It comes through a Child: the Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6).
Christ is our peace; he breaks down the walls of hostility (Ephesians 2:14).
points.apply: Ask the Child tonight for the gift of an inner peace that does not depend on circumstances.

sub: Families divided over property, words or old hurts.
Brothers who have not spoken for years.
Couples who live under one roof but far apart.
points.apply: Before the Christmas meal is over, take one step towards someone you are not at peace with.

points.h: Makers of peace in the world
sub: Pray for peace in the Holy Land and wherever there is war.
Refuse hatred and division on social media.
Blessed are the peacemakers (Matthew 5:9).
points.apply: Pray each day of the Christmas season for one country at war.

concl: The angels sang peace on earth among those whom God favours. God's favour rests on all who receive his Son. At this Holy Mass, let us exchange the sign of peace with sincerity, and carry it home.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will make peace with one person, and pray daily for one nation at war.
homily: Dear friends, on the night of the Nativity the shepherds heard the angels sing: glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace among those whom he favours (Luke 2:14). Glory to God and peace on earth go together. When God is given his glory, peace follows.

Isaiah had called the Child the Prince of Peace (Isaiah 9:6). Strange prince: born in a stable, laid in a manger, threatened by a king. Yet he brings what no army can bring. St Paul says: he is our peace; in his flesh he has broken down the dividing wall of hostility (Ephesians 2:14).

The world longs for peace. Tonight we pray for the land where Jesus was born, for all places torn by war, and for our own country wherever communities are divided. Christmas is not a holiday from the world's pain; it is God entering it.

But peace begins closer. In many families tonight there is an empty chair, not because of death, but because of a quarrel. Brothers who do not speak, sisters divided over property, a son estranged from his father. The Child in the manger asks: will you let me bring peace into your home?

Jacob, after twenty years of fear, ran to meet his brother Esau, and Esau embraced him (Genesis 33:4). Jesus taught: if your brother has something against you, go first and be reconciled (Matthew 5:24). Christmas is the best time to take that first step: a phone call, a visit, a slice of cake carried across the road.

At this Holy Mass, when we offer one another the sign of peace, let it be real. And let us go home as peacemakers, for blessed are the peacemakers; they will be called children of God (Matthew 5:9). A blessed and peaceful Christmas to all. Amen.

opts.a: Good news to the shepherds: Christ comes to the poor and the margins
intro: The first to hear the news of Christmas were not kings or priests, but shepherds: poor, rough, often despised, working through the night. God chose them as the first witnesses of his Son (Luke 2:8–12).
Christmas is good news for all who live at the edges: migrant workers, night-shift nurses, fishermen, farmers, the homeless and the forgotten.

sub: Shepherds were poor and considered unclean.
Yet David, the shepherd boy, became king.
The Good Shepherd is announced first to shepherds.
points.apply: Remember that God's first messengers went to those the world overlooks.

sub: The sign was not power, but a baby in a manger.
God meets us in poverty and simplicity.
The shepherds recognised him because he was like them.
points.apply: Look for Christ this Christmas in a poor person near you.

points.h: They went with haste and told others
sub: The shepherds did not keep the news to themselves.
They returned glorifying and praising God.
The poor became the first evangelisers.
points.apply: Share the joy of Christmas with someone who has no one to celebrate with.

concl: The Child who came first to shepherds comes now to us at this Holy Mass. Let us welcome him with simple hearts, and go out like the shepherds to tell others what we have seen.
opts.resolve: This Christmas I will share a meal or a gift with a migrant worker, a night worker or a poor family.
homily: Dear friends, on that first Christmas night, while Bethlehem slept, shepherds were keeping watch over their flocks in the fields. To them, not to the powerful in Jerusalem or Rome, an angel appeared and said: do not be afraid; I am bringing you good news of great joy for all the people (Luke 2:10).

Shepherds in those days were poor and often looked down upon. Their work kept them away from the Temple and from respectable company. Yet God chose them. The prophet Ezekiel had promised that God himself would shepherd his people, seek the lost and bind up the injured (Ezekiel 34:11–16). The Good Shepherd announces himself first to shepherds.

The sign they were given was not a palace or a crown, but a child wrapped in bands of cloth and lying in a manger (Luke 2:12). The poor recognised him because he was poor like them. God did not come to the world from above, but from below.

Think of the shepherds of our time: the migrant worker from another state who builds our houses, the nurse on night duty in a hospital abroad, the fisherman at sea on Christmas night, the security guard at the gate, the family in a rented room. Christmas is first their feast.

The shepherds went with haste, found Mary and Joseph and the child, and then made known what had been told them. They returned glorifying and praising God (Luke 2:16–20). The poor became the first evangelists. They had nothing to give but their joy, and it was enough.

At this Holy Mass, Christ comes to us as he came to the shepherds: simply, humbly. Let us receive him, and then, like them, go out with haste: to share our Christmas food, to visit someone alone, to bring good news to the margins. A joyful Christmas to all. Amen.

opts.a: A Christmas homily for families and children
intro: This homily is written for a congregation with many children and families. It uses simple words and three images the children can remember: the star, the crib and the gift.
Christmas is a family feast because God chose to be born into a family.

points.h: The star: God shows the way
sub: The star led the wise men to Jesus.
Our Christmas stars remind us: Jesus is the light.
Parents are stars for their children, showing the way to God.
points.apply: Let each family pray together tonight under the Christmas star.

sub: The great God became a little baby.
He chose a poor family and a simple place.
He wants a place in our homes and hearts.
points.apply: Let the children place the Child in the home crib with a prayer.

sub: At Christmas we give gifts because God gave us Jesus.
The best gift is love: time, kindness, forgiveness.
Jesus gives himself again at the Holy Mass.
points.apply: Let each person give one gift of love tomorrow that costs no money.

concl: The star shows the way, the crib shows God's humility, and the gift shows his love. May every family leave this Holy Mass with the Child in their hearts.
opts.resolve: Our family will pray together before the crib every evening until the end of the Christmas season.
homily: Dear children and dear families, a very happy Christmas to you! Tonight I want to talk about three things you can see around you: the star, the crib and the gift.

First, the star. Look at the stars shining in our homes and in the church. Long ago a star led the wise men to the place where Jesus was (Matthew 2:9–10). Our stars remind us that Jesus is the light of the world. And, dear parents, you are stars for your children: by your prayer and your example, you show them the way to Jesus.

Second, the crib. Look at the crib: Mary, Joseph, the shepherds, the animals, and the little baby. Isn't it amazing? The great God, who made the sun and the stars and the sea, became a tiny baby. He did not choose a palace; he was laid in a manger because there was no room in the inn (Luke 2:7). Children, Jesus wants a place in your home and in your heart. Will you make room for him?

Third, the gift. Why do we give gifts at Christmas? Because God gave us the best gift: his own Son. God so loved the world that he gave his only Son (John 3:16). So our gifts are a little copy of God's love. But the best gifts do not come from a shop: a hug, helping at home, saying sorry, sharing with a poor child.
And there is one more gift. At this Holy Mass, Jesus gives himself to us again. The baby of Bethlehem comes to us in Holy Communion. Bethlehem means house of bread, and Jesus is the Bread of Life.

So when you go home tonight, look at the star and say: Jesus, you are my light. Look at the crib and say: Jesus, come into my heart. And give one gift of love tomorrow. A happy and holy Christmas to every family. Amen.
Dear brothers and sisters, two days ago we knelt before the manger. Today the Church asks us to look around the manger: at Mary, at Joseph, at the family into which God chose to be born.

God could have come in any way he wished. He chose to come as a baby, into a family. He needed a mother to feed him, a father to protect him and teach him a trade, and a home where he could grow. That tells us how much God values the family.

Today's first reading shows Abraham and Sarah, old and childless. God tells Abraham to count the stars: so many will be your descendants. And Abraham believed. A family is not built first on property, jobs or plans, but on faith in God.

In the Gospel, Mary and Joseph bring Jesus to the Temple. They are poor; they can only offer two small birds. Simeon takes the child in his arms and praises God, but also tells Mary that a sword will pierce her heart. Even the Holy Family knew sorrow, fear and uncertainty. If your family is going through hard times, you are not far from Nazareth.

Then the Gospel says simply: they went home to Nazareth, and the child grew, filled with wisdom, and the favour of God was upon him. Thirty quiet years of work, prayer and ordinary love. That is where holiness grows for most of us: at the kitchen table, at work, in patience with each other.
So let us bring our families to the Lord today. Let us pray together at home, forgive each other quickly, respect our elders and bless our children. Jesus, Mary and Joseph, make our homes like yours.
kids: Children, Jesus had a family too: Mary his mother and Joseph his foster father.
He helped Joseph in the carpenter's shop and helped Mary at home.
He obeyed them and grew big and strong and wise.
How can you help at home this week? Maybe tidy your room, or help set the table, with a smile!

intro: St Joseph never speaks a single word in the Gospels, yet he protects the Holy Family at every danger.

sub: Four dreams, four obediences (Matthew 1:20; 2:13, 19, 22).
He rose and did as he was told.
Listening to God in silence.
points.apply: Spend five minutes in silence with God each day.

sub: Flight to Egypt by night (Matthew 2:13–15).
Work and sacrifice for wife and child.
Fathers as guardians of the home.
points.apply: Fathers: bless your children tonight.

sub: Just: faithful to God's law with mercy (Matthew 1:19).
He did not expose Mary to shame.
Justice and tenderness together.
points.apply: Correct with gentleness, never with humiliation.

concl: Joseph shows how to guard a family: with silence, obedience, work and tenderness.
Every family can ask St Joseph to be its protector.
opts.resolve: Our family will consecrate itself to the protection of St Joseph this week.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this feast of the Holy Family let us look at the one member who never says a word in the Gospels: St Joseph. Mary speaks, Jesus speaks, angels speak, but Joseph only listens and acts.

Four times an angel speaks to Joseph in a dream, and four times he obeys at once: to take Mary as his wife, to flee to Egypt, to return to the land of Israel, and to settle in Nazareth (Matthew 1:20; 2:13, 19, 22). Each time the Gospel says simply that Joseph got up and did as he was told. In a world full of noise, Joseph teaches us to listen to God in silence and to act without delay.

Joseph was a protector. When Herod sought to kill the child, Joseph took the child and his mother by night and fled to Egypt (Matthew 2:14). Think of that journey: a refugee family, poor, in a foreign land, with a little baby. Joseph worked with his hands to feed them. Today many fathers work far from home, in the Gulf or abroad, to support their families. Joseph understands them.

The Gospel calls Joseph a just man (Matthew 1:19). When he discovered that Mary was with child, he did not want to expose her to public disgrace. His justice was full of mercy. In our families too, justice and tenderness must go together: correction without humiliation, firmness without harshness, forgiveness without weakness.

Fathers, look at Joseph: protect your families, work honestly, pray, bless your children. Mothers, look at Mary. Children, look at Jesus, who was obedient to His parents. And let every family here entrust itself to St Joseph, guardian of the Redeemer. May he who guarded the Holy Family guard ours too.

opts.a: Teaching homily: the Christian family as domestic church
intro: The Church calls the family a domestic church. What does that mean in practice?

sub: Lumen Gentium 11: the family as domestic church.
Parents as first teachers of the faith (CCC 1656).
Prayer, Word, sacraments at the centre.
points.apply: Begin or renew daily family prayer.

sub: Honour your father and mother (CCC 2214–2220).
Parents' duty to educate in faith and virtue (CCC 2221–2226).
Care for elderly parents.
points.apply: Visit or call an elderly relative this week.

sub: Migration, screens, addiction, broken marriages.
The Holy Family also faced danger and exile.
The parish as family of families.
points.apply: Eat at least one meal a day together without phones.

concl: The family is where faith is first received, prayed and lived.
Nazareth is a school for every family.
opts.resolve: Our family will pray together every evening and share one meal a day without phones.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the Second Vatican Council gave the Christian family a beautiful name: the domestic church (Lumen Gentium 11). On the feast of the Holy Family, let us see what this means in practice.

A church is a place where God is worshipped, His Word is heard and love is lived. The home is meant to be exactly that. Parents are the first heralds of the faith for their children (CCC 1656). Long before catechism class, children learn from their parents how to make the sign of the cross, how to fold their hands, how to forgive. Moses told the Israelites to speak of God's words at home and on the road, when lying down and when rising (Deuteronomy 6:7).

The Fourth Commandment teaches children to honour their father and mother, with respect, gratitude, obedience while they are young, and care for them when they are old (CCC 2214–2220; Sirach 3:1–14). It also gives parents duties: to educate their children in faith, in prayer and in virtue, to respect their vocation, and to give the example of a good life (CCC 2221–2226). St Paul writes: fathers, do not provoke your children, or they may lose heart (Colossians 3:21).

Families today are under great pressure: work far from home, financial stress, screens that keep everyone apart in the same room, addiction, broken marriages. The Holy Family also knew danger, poverty and exile. They survived because God was at the centre. Let our families do the same: pray together every evening, even briefly; eat at least one meal a day together without phones; come to the Holy Mass together on Sunday; forgive before sleeping.

And let the parish be a family of families, supporting those who are struggling, single parents, widows, the elderly living alone. May Jesus, Mary and Joseph bless every family in this parish, and make our homes true domestic churches.

Dear brothers and sisters, today in the middle of Advent we celebrate Mary Immaculate. Some think this feast is about Jesus' conception, but it is about Mary's own conception in her mother's womb. From that first moment God preserved her from original sin.
Why? Because God was preparing a home for his Son. When we expect an important guest, we prepare the house. God prepared the most beautiful home: a soul without any stain of sin.

The first reading takes us to the garden. After the first sin, God calls, “Where are you?” And then he gives the first promise: the woman and her offspring will crush the serpent's head. Mary is that woman. The serpent never had power over her.

But don't think Mary did not need Jesus. She was saved by Jesus too, only in a more wonderful way. We are pulled out of the mud after we fall; Mary was kept from falling. Both are the work of the same Saviour.

And grace did not make Mary a robot. When the angel greeted her, “Full of grace, the Lord is with you,” she asked questions, she thought, and then she freely said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord.” Eve said no to God; Mary said yes. St Irenaeus said: Eve tied the knot; Mary untied it.

What God did in Mary from the first moment, he wants to do in us through Baptism, Confession and the Eucharist. Paul says God chose us “to be holy and blameless before him in love”. So today, let us answer God's question, “Where are you?”, honestly. Let us come to Confession, and with Mary say: “Let it be with me according to your word.”
kids: Children, today is Mary's special feast! God made Mary pure and beautiful from the very beginning.
Why? Because she was going to be Jesus' mother, and God wanted a perfect home for his Son.
When the angel came, Mary said: “Yes, God, I will do what you want.”
Today, bring flowers to Mary and say a Hail Mary with your family!

opts.a: Mary, the new Eve and the Ark of the Covenant
intro: The Fathers of the Church loved to read the Old Testament with Mary in mind. Two images help us understand this feast: the new Eve and the Ark.

sub: Eve listened to the serpent; Mary listened to the angel.
Eve's disobedience brought death; Mary's obedience opened the way to life.
St Irenaeus: the knot of Eve was untied by Mary.
points.apply: When tempted, say Mary's words: let it be done according to your word.

sub: The Ark held the tablets, the manna and Aaron's rod (Hebrews 9:4).
Mary carried the Word, the Bread of Life, the eternal Priest.
The Ark was made pure; Mary was preserved from all stain.
points.apply: Receive Christ in the Holy Mass with a clean heart, like Mary.

sub: God prepared a pure dwelling for His Son.
Mary was redeemed in a more exalted way.
What God did for her, He wants to begin in us.
points.apply: Make a good confession before Christmas.

concl: Mary Immaculate shows us what grace can do and what we are called to be.
The feast in Advent prepares a clean dwelling for Christ in us.
opts.resolve: Before Christmas I will make a good confession to prepare a clean dwelling for Christ.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the early Christians did not have the dogma of the Immaculate Conception in its later words, but they had a deep intuition about Mary, drawn from the Scriptures. Let us look at two images that the Fathers loved: Mary as the new Eve, and Mary as the Ark of the Covenant.

In the garden, Eve listened to the serpent and believed his lie. Through her disobedience, sin and death entered the world. But God promised that the offspring of a woman would crush the serpent's head (Genesis 3:15). In Nazareth another woman listened, not to a serpent but to an angel, and said: here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word (Luke 1:38). St Irenaeus wrote that the knot of Eve's disobedience was untied by Mary's obedience. Where Eve said no, Mary said yes.

The second image is the Ark of the Covenant. God commanded Moses to make it of acacia wood, covered with pure gold inside and out (Exodus 25:10–11). Inside were the tablets of the law, a jar of manna and Aaron's rod (Hebrews 9:4). When the Ark entered a house, it brought blessing; David danced before it. Mary carried in her womb the Word of God, the true Bread from heaven and the eternal High Priest. When she entered Elizabeth's house, the child leaped for joy (Luke 1:41). If the Ark had to be pure gold, how much more the living Ark of the Son of God.

This is what the Church proclaims today: that from the first moment of her conception Mary was preserved from every stain of original sin, by a singular grace of God and in view of the merits of Jesus Christ. She too was saved by her Son, but in a more exalted way: preserved rather than cleansed.

And what God did perfectly for Mary, He wants to begin in us. In Baptism we were washed; in confession we are cleansed again; in the Holy Mass we receive Christ as Mary did. This Advent, let us prepare a clean dwelling for Him. Make a good confession before Christmas, and ask Mary Immaculate to teach you to say yes.

opts.a: Teaching homily: the dogma of the Immaculate Conception
intro: Many people confuse this feast with the virginal conception of Jesus. Let us be clear about what the Church teaches and why.

sub: Defined by Pope Pius IX in 1854 (Ineffabilis Deus).
Mary was preserved from original sin from the first moment of her conception (CCC 491).
By a singular grace, in view of the merits of Christ.
points.apply: Learn the difference between the Immaculate Conception and the Virgin Birth.

sub: The angel's greeting: kecharitomene, highly favoured, filled with grace (Luke 1:28).
Mary was redeemed by her Son (CCC 492).
She remained free of personal sin all her life (CCC 493).
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly, attentive to the words full of grace.

points.h: Lourdes and the faith of the people
sub: 1858: I am the Immaculate Conception.
Eastern tradition: Mary the All-Holy, Panagia (CCC 493).
Our own Churches' devotion to Mary.
points.apply: Honour Mary this Advent with the Rosary.

concl: The dogma honours Christ, whose grace made Mary all-holy.
Mary Immaculate is the model and mother of the Church.
opts.resolve: This week I will pray the Rosary and ask Mary to make my heart pure.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, many Catholics think that today's feast is about the conception of Jesus in Mary's womb. It is not. That we celebrate on 25 March, the Annunciation. Today we celebrate the conception of Mary herself in the womb of her mother, whom tradition names Anne.

On 8 December 1854, Pope Pius IX solemnly defined that the most Blessed Virgin Mary, from the first moment of her conception, by a singular grace and privilege of almighty God, and in view of the merits of Jesus Christ the Saviour of the human race, was preserved free from all stain of original sin (CCC 491). Every word matters. Singular grace: it was God's gift, not Mary's achievement. In view of the merits of Jesus Christ: Mary too was saved by her Son.

Where is this in the Bible? The angel greets Mary as full of grace (Luke 1:28). The Greek word means one who has been, and remains, filled with God's favour. The Church understood that the woman chosen to be the Mother of God was prepared by grace from the beginning. The Catechism says that Mary was redeemed from the moment of her conception, and that by God's grace she remained free of every personal sin her whole life long (CCC 492–493). The Eastern Fathers call her Panagia, the All-Holy.

Four years after the definition, in 1858, Our Lady appeared to a poor girl, Bernadette, at Lourdes. When Bernadette asked her name, she answered: I am the Immaculate Conception. Bernadette did not understand the words, but the parish priest did. Heaven confirmed what the Church had taught.

Why does this matter? Because it shows what God's grace can do. Mary is not a goddess; she is a creature, entirely filled with grace. She shows what the Church is called to become: holy and without blemish (Ephesians 5:27). So let us honour her this Advent with the Rosary, and ask her to help us prepare for her Son at this Holy Mass and at Christmas.
Dear brothers and sisters, yesterday we sang carols around the crib. Today the priest wears red, and we hear about stones and death. Why?

An ancient bishop, St Fulgentius, explained: “Yesterday Christ was born on earth so that today Stephen might be born in heaven.” The Child of Bethlehem came to give his life. Christmas is the beginning of a love that will go all the way to the Cross, and those who follow him are invited into that same love.

Stephen was a deacon, chosen to serve the poor widows at table. He was also full of the Holy Spirit and spoke with such wisdom that no one could answer him. When they dragged him out to stone him, he looked up and saw heaven open and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.

And listen to his last words: “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” And: “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” These are almost exactly the words of Jesus on the Cross. Stephen died the way Jesus died, forgiving.

Standing there, holding the coats of those who threw the stones, was a young man named Saul. He later became St Paul, the great apostle. St Augustine said: “If Stephen had not prayed, the Church would not have had Paul.” Forgiveness is never wasted.

So this Christmas, let us ask: is there someone I need to forgive? A family member, a neighbour, a colleague? Let us pray for them by name, as Stephen did. And let us remember the Christians who suffer for their faith today. The joy of Christmas is strong enough to face even this.
kids: Children, today is the feast of St Stephen. He loved Jesus very much.
He helped poor people and told everyone about Jesus. Some people got angry and threw stones at him.
But Stephen did something amazing: he forgave them, just like Jesus did on the Cross.
Is there someone you need to forgive? Say: “Jesus, help me forgive.”

opts.a: Stephen, the deacon who served tables
intro: Before he was a martyr, Stephen was a deacon chosen to serve the widows (Acts 6:1–6).

sub: Complaints about neglected widows.
Seven men of good standing, full of the Spirit and wisdom.
Service is the school of holiness.
points.apply: Serve someone in your family without being asked.

sub: Faithful in small service, powerful in witness (Acts 6:8).
His face like an angel (Acts 6:15).
Wisdom no one could withstand (Acts 6:10).
points.apply: Let your service speak before your words.

sub: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit (Acts 7:59).
Lord, do not hold this sin against them (Acts 7:60).
The young man Saul was watching.
points.apply: Forgive one person this Christmas season.

concl: Stephen's martyrdom grew out of daily service and constant prayer.
The Christmas Child is the reason Stephen could forgive.
opts.resolve: This Christmas season I will serve someone humbly and forgive someone fully.
